rows.reason: Line 1 'spring-cleaning his little home' is the evidence; aching back correctly placed at line 4 as an effect of the work.
Quote 'all over his black fur' is on line 4; dust correctly at line 3; grass (l.15) and blue/white paint (l.60-61) are later.

'The carriage-drive is earlier' treats it as a place the Mole passed. Line 10 only compares his tunnel to a carriage-drive owned by other animals, so this reinforces the literal reading the distractor is tagged for (en-figurative-taken-literally). Say the tunnel is only being compared to a carriage-drive.
Quote spans lines 22-23 verbatim; correctly separates what the rabbit wants from the privilege; 'Onion-sauce!' at line 25 is the Mole's.
'Never in his life' and 'had he seen a river before' are on line 29; the animal at line 30 is the river.
Line 43 'seemed to twinkle' verbatim and is the first thing seen in the hole; face (l.48) and ears (l.51) come later.
Line 8 quote 'wore a blue coat and rode a black horse' verbatim; money (l.29) and manners (l.24-25) are later.
Line 11 says 'obliged to be in town the following day'; town = London is supported by line 16; accurate.
'only five altogether' spans lines 21-22 inside the cited range; removing Mr Bingley from the five gives the key; lines 17-20 are reports.

Final clause 'every dance belongs to Mr Bingley' reads literally as false or confusing (Darcy danced two). It means the 'every dance' option describes Mr Bingley; say so plainly, e.g. 'danced every dance' at line 37 is about Mr Bingley.
Quote 'obliged, by the scarcity of gentlemen, to sit down' is on line 47; scarcity glossed correctly; Darcy's words are later.
Lines 5-6 support 'without looking at her'; line 6 'Had he looked' correctly handles the negation-dropped option.
Lines 17-18: not a girl, a boy, Mrs Spencer bringing him; all true; separates Mrs Spencer from the stationmaster.
Lines 20-21 'came off the train with that girl' and 'gave her into my charge'; 'who handed over whom' targets the reversal option.
Lines 48-49: one hand on the carpet-bag, the other held out; correctly rules out 'both hands'.
Lines 64-65 'Come along' and 'Give me your bag' in one speech; accurate.
Lines 2-3 'so light' and 'the high wheels ran along so pleasantly' are the two reasons; accurate.
Lines 10-11: 'rising fast' and feared 'a bad night'; broken bridge is at line 47.
Sounds on lines 22-23, 'an oak' on line 23, 'torn up by the roots' runs to line 24; accurate.

'That adds a good six miles to the way home' is not what line 30 says. The text says it 'will be a good six miles before we get round to the wooden bridge again', i.e. the detour round to the bridge is six miles, not six miles added to the journey home.
Lines 55-58: bridge giving way, strong current, no light, 'more than likely we should all have been drowned'; accurate.
Lines 8-9: coat off, girl sent for 'sixpen'orth of nails', a boy after her about the size; accurate.

'He carries kind regards and a question about the leg' misdescribes line 13: 'hopes his leg's better' is a hope, not a question, and the only question is the spirit-level. It also does not show whose leg, which is what the attribute-transfer option turns on.
Lines 18-19: lifts, drops, out of the frame, tries to save the glass and cuts himself (finger tied up at l.24); accurate.
Lines 43-45: string slips, slides on to the piano, head and body strike all the notes; accurate.
Lines 49-51: let her know in time, make arrangements, a week with her mother; accurate.
Lines 7-9: named to first box, unnamed to second, bin bag for soles coming off; accurate.
Lines 24-25: warehouse, Leeds or near it, then out to shops; two stages accurate.
Lines 34-36: takes paper out, looks at the edge, puts it back without opening; accurate.

'What he likes about it is getting out of spellings' claims a feeling the passage does not state, and splits 'get out of spellings' off from Miss's words when line 41 has it inside the same reported sentence ('Miss said we can do that one on Monday and get out of spellings').
Lines 33-34: Friday box, low down under the swimming things, pushed flat level with the rest; accurate.
Lines 1-2 'pulling her hair gently, but quite enough'; shouting is at line 4 after Phyllis speaks; accurate.
Lines 4-7 are one speech; the reason is 'have everything beautiful before Mother gets up'; guides without stating the key.

'It tells you what they stand beneath' claims something line 9 does not say: they 'washed ... under the spout', nothing about standing. Also 'find the word under' is unquoted, so a child can read it as an instruction to look underneath; quote it ('under').
'find the two things they borrow' is false: the ash-tray and baking-tin are their own things used in place of the right ones (lines 21-22), not borrowed from anyone.
Line 54 note from Mrs Viney; son-in-law's arm (l.54-55); asks the child to read whose arm without stating it; line 55 gives ten o'clock.
Line 1: reason follows 'because' after the comma, nowhere to turn round; line 5 fact is separate; accurate.
Lines 4-5: four years of meaning to go versus twice getting as far as the caravan park; accurate.
Line 14 'nothing on her wall but a calendar from the surgery' is the reason; accurate.

'Go to line 20 and find the word below' and 'notice further along' leave the cited words unquoted, so 'find the word below' reads as an instruction to look below the line. Quote them ('Below', 'further along'); content is otherwise correct.
Line 37 buoy 'knocks when the water moves'; line 38 'nothing musical' and 'I decided that was what she had always meant'; accurate.
